user_prompt: What is the effect of remotely delivered cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT; internet-based, telephone-based, app-based or video-delivered, including acceptance and commitment or exposure-based variants with a cognitive-behavioural basis), compared with treatment as usual or a waiting-list control, on functional disability at the end of treatment in adults with chronic non-headache pain (for example low back pain, fibromyalgia, osteoarthritis or mixed chronic pain)?  Effect measure: pool as a standardised mean difference (SMD, Hedges' g) using a random-effects model. SMD < 0 means less disability with CBT (favours CBT).  Outcome: functional disability or physical functioning, extracted as the post-treatment mean, SD and number of participants per arm. - Use one disability or physical-function measure per trial, preferring a disability-specific scale (for example the Roland-Morris Disability Questionnaire, Pain Disability Index, Oswestry, WHO-DAS or similar) over a general quality-of-life subscale; if only a general physical-function subscale is reported (for example SF-36 or SF-12 physical function), use that. - Direction: on disability scales a higher score means more disability. On physical-function scales (for example SF-36, SF-12 physical function) a higher score means better function. Reverse the sign of the means of scales where higher is better (multiply by −1) so that a lower value always means less disability, before computing the SMD. - Use the first assessment after the treatment ended (post-treatment; typically 3 to 24 weeks after randomisation). Do not use longer follow-up assessments. - If variability is reported as SE or SEM, convert to SD = SE × √n. Check table footnotes for whether "±" is SD or SE. - Control: treatment as usual, waiting list, or usual care plus waiting list. Exclude trials whose control is an active therapy (for example another psychological treatment or an attention control). - Multi-arm trials: if there are several remote CBT arms (for example with different levels of therapist contact), combine them into one CBT group (pool means and SDs, sum participants) and compare with the shared control once. - Use the number randomised or analysed as reported; assign arms by treatment description, not by column position. - Include only randomised controlled trials of remotely delivered CBT in adults. Exclude face-to-face therapy, trials in children, and headache or migraine trials.  Do not pool pain intensity, pain improvement, quality of life, mood, anxiety, adverse events or any outcome other than functional disability.
